title: The 5-Minute Rule: Why You Can’t Start Tasks
description:
Procrastination isn't about laziness, it's about emotional regulation. Learn how the 5-minute rule bypasses your brain's resistance to get things done.

#productivity #psychology #focus #habits

hook.narration: Procrastination is rarely a time management problem. It is actually a way of managing your difficult emotions.
hook.subtitle: It is about managing your feelings

visual.description: A close-up of a person looking stressed at a desk with soft blue lighting.

scenes.narration: Your brain avoids tasks because they feel boring, difficult, or overwhelming. It tries to protect you from that discomfort by scrolling through your phone instead.
scenes.subtitle: Avoiding the pain of starting

visual.description: A glowing human brain with digital neural pathways against a dark background.

scenes.narration: The 5-minute rule is simple. Commit to working on a task for exactly 5 minutes, but give yourself real, honest permission to stop once that timer hits zero.
scenes.subtitle: A tiny window of commitment

visual.description: A minimalist mechanical kitchen timer on a clean white table.

scenes.narration: Starting is the hardest part for our brains. Once you break the seal, momentum kicks in and your brain naturally wants to finish what it has already started.
scenes.subtitle: The hardest part is behind you

visual.description: A single drop of water hitting a calm pool creating ripples.

scenes.narration: Imagine a messy kitchen or a 10-page report. Thinking about the whole project is painful, but anyone can wash just five plates or write three sentences in 300 seconds.
scenes.subtitle: Small wins lead to big results

visual.description: A stack of clean dishes sitting by a sunlit window.

scenes.narration: To make this work, you must set a visible timer, make the first step tiny and specific, and remove friction by putting your phone in another room.
scenes.subtitle: How to master the rule

visual.description: A notebook with three clean checkmarks on a wooden desk.

scenes.narration: Lowering the barrier to entry tricks your brain into action without the fear of failure. Follow for one new idea every day.
scenes.subtitle: Action beats perfection every time

visual.description: A macro shot of a green sprout growing out of dry soil.
